restaurant_name: เวชพิสิษฐ์ คลินิกเวชกรรม
text: I went to the doctor today because I had a very sore throat. The doctor asked if I wanted an injection, which I didn't want. I just wanted some throat medication and a throat spray. The doctor said I should buy the medicine myself. I didn't want to pay for it myself because without a certificate and receipt, I couldn't claim it from my company. If I lived near Sattahip, I would use my social security insurance. But this doctor refused treatment and prescribed medication. Why should I pay when I have company benefits that only cover a one-time expense? The doctor spoke as if I wasn't sick. Doctors here are strange.

text:
I went around looking for a pharmacy to see a doctor, but once inside, the expression on their face, the answers to my simple questions 😑, and the examination... I decided to go back to the pharmacy instead.
I think one visit is enough. …

restaurant_name: เวชพิสิษฐ์ คลินิกเวชกรรม
text: The doctor asked about my symptoms as if they didn't want to treat me, and their tone was very unwelcoming. I'm a patient who needs treatment; I'm paying for it, not getting it for free. I sat there answering questions for less than a minute before they told me to go get medication. This was my second time receiving treatment here; the first time was bad, but I didn't expect this to be this bad. And the treatment is very expensive; the consultation wasn't even worth it. This will be my first and last time at this clinic.

restaurant_name: เวชพิสิษฐ์ คลินิกเวชกรรม
text: If there's a reason for not allowing the examination or treatment, please inform the patient using a more polite tone and language.

restaurant_name: เวชพิสิษฐ์ คลินิกเวชกรรม
text: I was very dissatisfied with the service. I needed treatment for a severe sore throat, and they gave me Vitamin C, paracetamol, and muscle relaxants, but no antibiotics. I wouldn't give them even one star.
author_name: ปิ่นมนัส ขันติโยธาทิพย์

restaurant_name: เวชพิสิษฐ์ คลินิกเวชกรรม
text: The counter staff didn't know anything when I asked questions and gave no advice. As for the doctor, once I entered the room, they didn't tell me where the injection would be given; they just held the needle and waited, leaving me confused. I was wondering if it was in my arm or somewhere else. When I asked, they became rude and spoke dismissively. I paid for this treatment; it wasn't free. One visit is enough for this clinic. Bye!
